notes: Design: TreeMcts.redet = Some(Redet{root, me, every}) only when redeterminize_every>0 and search_seed is set (oracle/recorded-rng path falls back to off, like effective_worlds). Every `every` reads run_in_world redraws determinize_with(root_state, me, rng) from the ORIGINAL decide state and rebuilds the Session; the tree is kept. World i keeps its search rng (seed+i) and advances it. PV / commit continuation are built from world 0's initial sample as before. RunOut unchanged.

Off path: simulate() only branches into simulate_redet when redet is Some; descend() is now a wrapper over descend_inner(soft=false) with identical logic. Node gains `boxed` and `sigs` fields that the off path never reads. Bit-identity confirmed by Rust test (a), golden 3 tests, make test, and the m=100000 real-game check.

Reconciliation condition: spec said opponent turn or in_dialog. I used opponent turn OR any active_interaction() (superset of in_dialog). Reason: DIALOG_ACTIONS omits ARRANGE_DECK and SELECT_RESOURCE; ARRANGE_DECK can show the opponent's deck-top cards (world-dependent uuids) to me. Read rules/legal.rs and rules/pending.rs: my MAIN_ACTION (PLAY/ATTACK/ATTACH_DON/ACTIVATE_MAIN/TURN_END) depends on my own zones and the opponent's public field/leader; SELECT_BLOCKER/SELECT_COUNTER use my own field/hand; mulligan is mine. Opponent hidden cards reach my choices only through interactions (SEARCH_AND_SELECT over opponent hand/deck etc.), which the active_interaction condition catches.

Residual dependence on own nodes: the same move sequence can still lead to a different own-turn state in another world if an automatic (no-choice) effect reads the opponent's hidden cards (e.g. reveal opponent deck top). Safety net: on an unchecked own node, if the chosen move fails to apply, descend_inner(soft=true) returns None and simulate_redet switches to reconciliation for that visit and reselects (stat `unplayable`); only a move that is legal in this world yet fails to apply becomes a dead child (as before). Measured unplayable = 0 in all runs.

World/node mismatch guard: if the node's stored to_move differs from the current player in this world (or the world state is terminal), the sim evaluates this state as a leaf from the node's to_move perspective and does not touch the node's edges (stat `mismatch`, ~2-6% of visits). Stored terminal nodes keep their term_val (winner/life/deck counts are public, per spec 4).

New moves: appended to legal/p/n/w/children with p from one priors_keep over this world's full legal list (existing p untouched). Not added at the root (node 0) so the root stats keep world 0's order (merge_worlds/move_sig mapping), nor at boxed nodes. Duplicate move_sig within a node is matched by multiplicity (first unmatched).

Limitation (as specified): battle/dialog box folding is fixed by the first world that expanded the node; if the folded move is not legal in a later world the visit evaluates the leaf (stat `empty`, ~2-3% of visits). PUCT parent count at checked nodes = sum of n over candidates in this world.

Profiling: Determinize category already existed and now shows the redraw cost (m=1: 12.9 s over 1,284 decides = 637 redraws/decide incl. trivial decides; m=8: 1.9 s; m=64: 0.3 s). Extra legal_actions from reconciliation are under Legal (m=1 79 s vs m=0 51 s).

Surprise to verify in Phase 3 measurement: on identical positions m=8/64 are faster than m=0 (sum of decide time x0.75 / x0.70) and use fewer network evaluations per decide (n_value 3014 -> 1742/1806, n_priors 2265 -> 1280/1253). The m=100000 check shows the machinery is exact inside one world, so the drop comes from switching worlds. Hypothesis (not verified): visits at opponent nodes spread over more (world-specific) moves, so the tree is shallower and fewer leaves sit deep in battle windows that need quiesce resolution. Strength is not measured here (arena is a separate step).

Latency tool: tests/scripts/rs_decide_latency.py was listed as 'new' in plan §1 and did not exist; created it here (TEST_SPEC §3 row). Besides the per-arm independent-games form required by §7.1 it has --compare-every for same-position paired timing, which is the number to read because arms otherwise play different games (m=0 median 7.2 ms vs m=1 1.5 ms in independent games was a decision-mix artefact).
